model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the area of vineyards (in thousands of hectares) across seven countries from 2013 to 2022. The horizontal axis represents the years, while the vertical axis shows the vineyard area in thousands of hectares, ranging from 0 to 1200. Each year has a cluster of seven colored bars, representing Spain (blue), France (orange), China/continental (gray), Italy (yellow), Turkey (light blue), the USA (green), and Argentina (dark blue). Spain consistently has the largest vineyard area, with values fluctuating between approximately 970 and 990 thousand hectares. France follows with a slightly smaller area, ranging from about 780 to 820 thousand hectares. Italy's vineyard area is also significant, generally between 680 and 720 thousand hectares. The USA, Turkey, and Argentina have smaller but relatively stable vineyard areas, with the USA around 450-500 thousand hectares, Turkey around 400-450 thousand hectares, and Argentina around 200-250 thousand hectares. China/continental has the smallest area, consistently around 200-250 thousand hectares. Overall, the chart shows that Spain and France are the dominant vineyard areas, with relatively stable trends over the decade, while the other countries maintain smaller but consistent vineyard sizes.
